items.title: Rusty Dedrick interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998
items.q: I worked with Shep Fields. ... I had some friends from the Army who were working with Shep Fields’ band. ... So that’s what I did until I got my six months in. I worked it.

ctx.x: Bar mitzvahs and all kinds of stuff. © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-

Yes, absolutely. I took anything. I worked with Shep Fields. I got my three months in, in three months you’re not allowed to do anything, to get your card, three months on your transfer. The next three months you’re allowed to work with permission. And I had some friends from the Army who were working with Shep Fields’ band. I had never played that ricky-tick kind of, he called it “rippling rhythm.” And they were holding auditions. He was reorganizing his Rippling Rhythm band. They were holding auditions at Nola…
Well there you go. What didn’t he like about your hot playing? Do you know? I mean was it maybe too modern for him?
